newsitem.title: BELGIUM: West European car sales fall 1.9 percent in May.
newsitem.headline: West European car sales fall 1.9 percent in May.

text.p: West European car sales fell 1.9 percent in May compared with the same month last year, partly reflecting weaker-than-expected economic conditions, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association (ACEA) said Thursday.

The number of new car registrations fell to 1,151,900 from 1,174,500 in May 1996, with Germany, Europe's biggest market, recording a 12.9 percent drop to 295,000. Cumulative registrations for the first five months of the year were 0.3 percent higher at 5,855,100 units.
"It probably is a bit weaker than expected," said European car industry analyst Philip Ayton at investment bank Barclays de Zoete Wedd. "Without Italy it would have been pretty weak.

Italy stood out with a 43.2 percent jump in May registrations to 232,600, thanks to a national cash incentive programme which encourages motorists to turn in old cars for scrap in exchange for buying new models. The programme was introduced in January and will run until September.

Last month's decline in German registrations followed a 4 percent year-on-year gain in April. Heinz Handtrack, ACEA director of trade and economics, said the drop reflected the state of the economy and more public holidays in May this year than last year.

Sales in western Europe as a whole -- defined as the 15-nation European Union plus Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Norway -- showed a similar trend, as the 1.9 percent May drop came after a 9.3 percent April increase.
"I think the weaker economy affects nearly all European countries," Handtrack said.
ACEA is still sticking to an earlier forecast of sales growth of more than 2 percent for the full year, but Handtrack said it may be revised downward.
Ayton at Barclays de Zoete Wedd said he may also adjust down his forecast of 1997 growth of around 1.5 percent.
